problem:
The height $h$ (in feet) of a small rocket $t$ seconds after it is launched can be modeled by the function $h(t)=-16{t}^{2}+128t.$ Find the instantaneous rate at which the rocket's height is changing with respect to time at the moment when its height is equal to $256$ feet.

The instantaneous rate of change of the rocket's height when its height is $256$ feet is
{{field-1}} feet per second.
worked_solution:
Since we are given that the rocket's height is $256$ feet, the time can be calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}h(t) & =256 \\ -16{t}^{2}+128t & =256 \\ -16{t}^{2}+128t-256 & =0 \\ -16({t}^{2}-8t+16) & =0 \\ -16(t-4)^{2} & =0 \\ (t-4)^{2} & =0 \\ t-4 & =0 \\ t & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

The instantaneous rate at which the rocket's height is changing when $t=4$ seconds is equal to ${h}^{′}(4).$

Taking the derivative, the rate of change of $h(t)$ with respect to $t$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-16{t}^{2}+128t) \\  & =-32t+128,\end{aligned}
$$

and evaluating at $t=4$ gives

$$
{h}^{′}(4)=-32(4)+128=0.
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate at which the rocket's height is changing when $t=4$ seconds is $0$ feet per second.
